question: How does the analogy of the yogi clarify the roles of assisting causes and brothers in the lineage?
premises: A yogi may have capacity even without an assisting cause.
Brothers are described as born of one source.
Anyone similar to that shared-source relation can be counted in the same way.
inference: The lineage can include both exceptional independence and relations defined by shared origin or similarity.
uncertainties: The verse is highly compressed, and the exact mapping of 'brothers' to the earlier threefold structure is interpretive.
plain_english: Just as a yogi can have capacity even without an assisting cause, brothers are those born of one source; and anyone similar to that may also be counted in that way.
